details:
PHOENIX FIRE INTELLIGENCE

Team PHOENIX Orbit | NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

Project Overview

What if we could explore the science of fire beyond Earth's gravity?

PHOENIX FIRE INTELLIGENCE is an immersive scientific exploration platform designed to make microgravity combustion research more accessible, interactive, and understandable.

Developed for the Flame in Freefall challenge, our project combines 3D visualization, experimental data analysis, and artificial intelligence to transform complex NASA research into an engaging digital experience.

The Problem

Fire behaves differently in microgravity. Without normal buoyancy-driven convection, flame behavior depends on different interactions between oxygen availability, airflow, fuel properties, and heat transfer.

NASA has conducted important combustion experiments, including FLEX, SAFFIRE, and BASS-II. However, the resulting information is distributed across scientific datasets and technical documents, making it challenging for non-specialists to explore and compare.

Our Solution

PHOENIX brings scientific exploration and immersive storytelling together through:

  • Interactive 3D Experience: A cinematic journey featuring a plasma-inspired environment and animated transitions into a virtual research laboratory.
  • Scientific Data Dashboard: An interface for exploring 285 processed experiment records, evidence matrices, and data-quality annotations.
  • Experiment Exploration: Research-focused visualizations and comparisons involving FLEX and SAFFIRE.
  • PHOENIX AI: A Gemini-powered retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) prototype that retrieves information from scientific documents and generates answers with source and page references.
  • Accessible Scientific Communication: An experience designed to help students, researchers, and space enthusiasts engage with microgravity combustion research.

Technology

Our prototype uses React, TypeScript, Vite, Three.js, React Three Fiber, GSAP, Python, FastAPI, Google Gemini, and retrieval-augmented generation.

Impact and Future Vision

PHOENIX aims to bridge the gap between scientific data and public understanding. By connecting interactive visualization with research evidence, our platform provides a new way to explore the science behind fire safety in space.

Future development will focus on expanding the scientific database, completing the public deployment of backend services, improving AI integration, and introducing more advanced visual comparisons.

PHOENIX is a research and educational prototype, not an operational fire-risk prediction system.
